key_insight: MAGIC learns to build multi-agent collaboration graphs by choosing the right granularity for each role locally—either a single agent or a reusable group—rather than using one fixed organization style.
engineering_relevance: This enables more efficient and task-adaptive LLM agent systems, balancing coordination quality with inference cost in complex workflows.
method: Sequentially constructs an agent graph by selecting a functional role, instantiating it at mixed granularity, and attaching it to the current graph.
Uses dense-reward reinforcement learning with potential-based reward shaping to provide intermediate feedback during graph construction.
Optimizes the construction policy from trajectories sampled under the current policy while preserving the final task reward objective.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MAGIC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on eight benchmarks and shows strong inference efficiency in an efficiency study.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful reward shaping and probe-based signals, so performance may be sensitive to how well intermediate utilities and structural rewards are defined.
paper_title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
